label.description:
The label of the control. Any node is accepted, so it can carry a link, an
info trigger or other markup — the terms-and-conditions pattern.

Text doubles as the control's accessible name. A richer label does not, so
pass `ariaLabel` alongside it; a development-only warning says so when it
is missing.

ariaLabel.description:
Accessible name of the control, needed when `label` is not plain text.
Without it the name becomes whatever the label subtree computes to, which
for a label carrying a link or an icon reads as the wrong name or as none.

indeterminate.description: Only applies when `type` is `checkbox`; ignored for `radio`.

animation.description:
Animation applied to every skeleton item inside. Nested skeletons inherit
the animation of the closest skeleton that sets one, so a nested skeleton
can replace it or turn it off with `none`.

ariaLabel.description:
Text announced by screen readers while loading. The skeleton shapes are
hidden from assistive technology, so this is the only thing announced.
Ignored by nested skeletons.

color.description: Theme color for the skeleton items (`primary`, `secondary`, `info`, ...).

gap.description:
Space between items, and between the shapes of every item. Numbers are
pixels.

direction.description: Axis the items and their shapes are laid out on.

items.description:
Number of times the item is repeated. Setting it turns the skeleton into an
iterator: every repetition is wrapped in its own `.d-skeleton-slot`.
Capped at 100.

itemClassName.description: Class applied to the wrapper of every item.

children.description:
Template of each item, as a node or as a function receiving the index.
Without `items` and without a function, children render as-is.

width.description: Width of the block. Numbers are pixels.

height.description: Height of the block. Numbers are pixels.

rounded.description:
Border radius as a Bootstrap `rounded-*` utility. `true` maps to `rounded`,
`false` to `rounded-0`. When omitted, `--bs-skeleton-border-radius` applies.

useConfirmModal.description:
Hook to display a confirmation modal.

Renders into the portal node specified by `DConfirmModalContainer` (typically `#d-portal`).
The confirm modal floats above the portal stack and handles its own Escape key,
preventing interference with underlying modals.

Requires both `DContextProvider` wrapping your application AND an explicit
`<DConfirmModalContainer nodeId="d-portal" />` mounted in your app.
useConfirmModal.name: useConfirmModal

useCountdown.description:
Generic seconds-based countdown hook.

Starts counting down from `seconds` to `0` and exposes `restartCountdown`
to reset and restart the timer (e.g. for "resend code in Xs" patterns,
session-expiry banners, or any other cooldown/throttle UI).
useCountdown.name: useCountdown

useDContext.description:
Returns the Dynamic UI context value set by `DContextProvider`.
Falls back to the library's built-in defaults when no `DContextProvider`
is present in the tree — wrap your application with `DContextProvider`
to customise icons, currency, language, and portal settings.
useDContext.signature: useDContext() => { language, currency, icon, iconRegistry, iconMap, breakpoints, setContext }
useDContext.name: useDContext

useDPortalContext.description:
Hook to open/close registered portals (modals, offcanvas, etc.).

**Prerequisite**: must be called inside a `DContextProvider` configured with
`portalName` and `availablePortals`. `DContextProvider` mounts
`DPortalContextProvider` internally — consumers never use
`DPortalContextProvider` directly.
useDPortalContext.signature: useDPortalContext<T extends Record<string, unknown>>() => { stack, openPortal, closePortal }

stack.description: Currently open portals, ordered from oldest (bottom) to newest (top).

openPortal.description:
Pushes a named portal onto the stack, rendering its registered component
with the given payload.

closePortal.description: Pops the topmost portal off the stack, closing it.

useDPortalContext.name: useDPortalContext

useDToast.description:
Hook that provides a `toast` function to dispatch DToast notifications.

Prerequisites:
- The calling component must be inside `DContextProvider` (provides icon context).
- `DToastContainer` must be present somewhere in the component tree as a render target.

toast.description:
Dispatches a toast notification rendered as a `DToast` component.
When `data` is a `ToastData` object, the default DToast layout is used.
When `data` is a render function, full custom content is rendered instead.
Returns the toast ID, which can be passed to `reactHotToast.dismiss(id)`.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Toast content as `ToastData` or a render function for custom layouts.

parameters.name: toastProps
parameters.description: Optional per-toast overrides: id, duration, position.

useDToast.returnType: { toast: (data: ToastData | ValueFunction<Renderable, Toast>, toastProps?: DToastOptions) => string; }
useDToast.name: useDToast

useErrorBoundary.description:
Re-exported unchanged from `react-error-boundary`; see its documentation.

Convenience hook for imperatively showing or dismissing error boundaries.

⚠️ This hook must only be used within an `ErrorBoundary` subtree.

error.description: The currently visible `Error` (if one has been thrown).

resetBoundary.description: Method to reset and retry the nearest active error boundary (if one is active).

showBoundary.description:
Trigger the nearest error boundary to display the error provided.

ℹ️ React handles errors thrown while rendering.
Errors thrown in event handlers, or after async code has run, will not be caught automatically.
This method is a way to imperatively show the nearest error boundary for those errors.

useErrorBoundary.returnType: { error: unknown | null; resetBoundary: () => void; showBoundary: (error: unknown) => void; }
useErrorBoundary.name: useErrorBoundary

useInputCurrency.description:
State and handlers for a currency input: a formatted string while the field
is idle and the raw number while it is being edited.

`minValue`/`maxValue` bound the value. With `clamp` (default `true`) an
out-of-range value is brought into range whenever it is not being typed:
on mount, when `value` or the bounds change, and on blur. Every time the
clamp changes the value, `onChange` receives the clamped number, so the
input and the consumer's state never disagree. While the field is focused
the typed number is reported as is, so a partial entry is not rewritten.

With `clamp: false` the value is never changed: the bounds only feed
`isOverMax` / `isUnderMin`, so the consumer can show its own message (e.g.
"You exceeded the limit") and keep the entered amount.

Controlled usage follows the same contract as a native controlled input:
reflect `onChange` into `value` in the same event (`setState` in the
handler). The hook keeps showing `value` whenever it isn't being edited, so
a consumer can reject a change by keeping `value` as it was. Deferring the
update (a timer, awaiting a request) makes the hook see a stale `value` in
between: the field can flash the previous amount and a clamp can be
reported again when the deferred value arrives.
useInputCurrency.signature: useInputCurrency(currencyOptions: Options, value?: number, onFocus?: (event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void, onChange?: (value?: number) => void, onBlur?: (event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void, ref?: ForwardedRef<HTMLInputElement>, minValue?: number, maxValue?: number, clamp?: boolean) => { inputRef, innerValue, innerType, isOverMax, isUnderMin, handleOnFocus, handleOnChange, handleOnBlur }

current.description: The current value of the ref.

useInputCurrency.returnType: { inputRef: RefObject<HTMLInputElement | null>; innerValue: string; innerType: string; isOverMax: boolean; isUnderMin: boolean; handleOnFocus: (event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void; handleOnChange: (newValue?: string) => void; handleOnBlur: (event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void; }
useInputCurrency.name: useInputCurrency

useOtp.description:
Headless hook exposing the same OTP logic used internally by `DOtp`
(code state, length + correctness validation, submit action and resend
countdown), without any bundled markup/styles.

Use this when the default `DOtp` component doesn't match your design and
you need to build a fully custom UI while reusing the same behavior.

Internally composes `useCountdown` for the resend timer and re-exposes
`secondsLeft`/`restartCountdown`, so there is no need to call
`useCountdown` separately.

`invalid` becomes `true` both when the OTP is shorter than `otpSize` and
when `action` throws/rejects (e.g. the backend rejected the entered code
as incorrect). In the latter case, the thrown value is exposed as `error`
so custom UIs can render an appropriate message (e.g. "Invalid code" vs.
"Enter all digits"). `invalid`/`error` are cleared automatically as soon
as the user edits the code via `setOtp`.
useOtp.signature: useOtp({ action, otpSize = 6, seconds = 15 }: UseOtpConfig) => { otp, setOtp, invalid, error, submit, isLoading, secondsLeft, restartCountdown }

setOtp.description:
Updates the OTP value (wire this to your custom pin input's `onChange`).
Also clears `invalid`/`error` as soon as the value actually changes, so
the error state disappears once the user edits the code (a no-op call
with the same value, e.g. from an uncontrolled input re-notifying its
current value, does not reset `invalid`/`error`).

invalid.description:
`true` when `submit()` is called with an OTP shorter than `otpSize`, or
when `action` throws/rejects (e.g. the backend rejected the entered
code as incorrect).

error.description:
The value thrown/rejected by `action`, or `null` otherwise. Use it to
render a specific message for a wrong code, as opposed to a too-short
one.

submit.description:
Validates the OTP length; if valid, calls `action`. If `action`
rejects, the returned promise rejects too (so callers can still
`.catch()` it for logging), and `invalid`/`error` are set beforehand.

isLoading.description:
`true` while `action` is being awaited inside `submit()` (i.e. the OTP
passed the length check and the async action hasn't settled yet). Wire
it to your submit button's loading/disabled state. It's `false` while
idle and immediately after `action` settles (whether it resolves or
rejects), and it's never set to `true` for the too-short/length
validation failure since `action` isn't called in that case.

secondsLeft.description: Seconds remaining until resend is available.

restartCountdown.description: Restarts the resend countdown (call it from your "Resend" action).

useOtp.name: useOtp

useProvidedRefOrCreate.description:
There are some situations where we only want to create a new ref if one is not provided to a component
or hook as a prop. However, due to the `rules-of-hooks`, we cannot conditionally make a call to `React.useRef`
only in the situations where the ref is not provided as a prop.
This hook aims to encapsulate that logic, so the consumer doesn't need to be concerned with violating `rules-of-hooks`.

current.description: The current value of the ref.
